title: No reflow at 320 CSS pixels
user_impact: Users zooming to 400% must scroll in two directions — content becomes inaccessible.
technical_impact: Fixed widths or overflow:hidden prevent responsive reflow.

checks.source: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 Reflow (320 CSS px width; exception for content requiring two-dimensional layout)
checks.applicability: The page at a 320 x 256 CSS px viewport (run once after the mobile pass), except content that needs two-dimensional layout: data tables, images, maps, diagrams, video, application areas.
checks.expectation:
Fails when the document needs horizontal scrolling at 320 CSS px (scroll
width more than 5 px beyond the viewport) because of content that should
reflow; the finding names the widest such element. Exactly 320 px wide
content passes. A fixed width that only applies above 400 px does not apply
at 320 px. A width capped by script after load passes. Overflow caused only
by a data table, image or other 2D content is excepted by the criterion and
passes; a layout table (role=presentation/none) is not excepted. Overflowing
text without a wider element box (an unbroken string) still fails. A page
whose only wide content is such 2D content (visual_no_text: one image) has
nothing the criterion applies to.
